title: What Are You Going to Do?

sections.content: Ir a + infinitivo expresses an intention or a plan connected to the present. It is useful when preparation or a decision already exists.

items.spanish: Voy a cambiar de trabajo porque quiero aprender algo nuevo.
items.english: I'm going to change jobs because I want to learn something new.

items.spanish: Vamos a salir temprano para que no tengamos que esperar.
items.english: We're going to leave early so that we don't have to wait.

items.spanish: Marta va a estudiar en Chile el año que viene.
items.english: Marta is going to study in Chile next year.

items.spanish: Estamos a punto de empezar, así que prepara tus cosas.
items.english: We're about to start, so get your things ready.

sections.content: If you could already say *"I've decided..."* before opening your mouth, reach for *ir a* + infinitive — it presents a plan that exists in the speaker's mind before the moment of speaking, not a fresh guess about the future.
